# 1 Enoch Chapter 63 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 63:6 — 'our hope was in the scepter of our kingdom' — the indictment of earthly power

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "our-hope-was-in-the-scepter-of-our-kingdom, and-in-our-glory" | Literal; the Ge'ez qwetrat = scepter, rod of authority |
| LOGOS | "our hope was in the scepter of our kingdom, and in our glory" | Agrees exactly |
| PNEUMA | "Our hope was in the scepter of our kingdom and in our own glory" | Adds 'own' to 'our glory' for emphasis |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. 'The scepter of our kingdom' is the most pointed phrase in the Parables' critique of earthly power — the scepter is the precise symbol of royal authority. All three translators agree on the substance; PNEUMA's added 'own' is not in the Ge'ez.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Theologically central verse.

---

## 63:5 — 'Would that we had rest' — the irony of the kings' longing

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Would-that-we-had-rest to-glorify and-give-thanks" | Conditional/optative; expresses futile wish |
| LOGOS | "Would that we had rest to glorify and give thanks" | Preserves the optative |
| PNEUMA | "If only we had rest to glorify and give thanks" | 'If only' — same optative register |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Would that' and 'if only' are equivalent optatives; LOGOS's rendering is slightly more formal and suits the register of the prayer. The irony — that they now desire the worship they once refused — is preserved in all versions.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Minor stylistic divergence.

---

## 63:9 — 'burden of Sheol' — the nature of their descent

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "into-the-burden-of-Sheol" | Literal; Ge'ez massafit = burden, load, weight |
| LOGOS | "into the burden of Sheol" | Preserves 'burden' |
| PNEUMA | "into the weight of Sheol" | 'Weight' for 'burden' — closely synonymous |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'burden of Sheol' (EMET/LOGOS). 'Burden' is the slightly more precise translation of the Ge'ez massafit and captures the sense of oppressive weight that Sheol places on its inhabitants.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 63:12 — the fallen angels briefly reappear

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "These are-the-angels who-descended-to-the-earth, and-revealed-what-was-hidden" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "These are the angels who descended to the earth and revealed what was hidden to the children of men" | Preserves the identification |
| PNEUMA | "These are the angels who came down to earth and exposed hidden things to humanity" | 'Exposed hidden things' for 'revealed what was hidden'; 'humanity' for 'children of men' |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Revealed what was hidden to the children of men' preserves the Enochic language precisely — these are the Watchers of ch. 6-16, and the phrase 'children of men' (Ge'ez waluda sab') should not be collapsed to 'humanity' (PNEUMA).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
